body:
When a kid shuts down during a correction, they're not being difficult.
They're usually just processing feeling wrong in front of someone they want to impress.
That pause before they respond? Worth waiting through. 🤍

body:
Early writing is tricky to sequence — too much too soon and kids freeze, too little and they coast.
The whole structure of Mimi's First Sentences is built around that gap: enough support to feel safe, enough challenge to feel real.

body:
Repetition gets a bad reputation — but kids who ask to hear the same story seven nights in a row aren't being stubborn.
They're locking in patterns. Rhythm, sequence, what comes next.
That loop IS the learning. The novelty comes later, once the foundation feels solid. 🧩

body:
Write a sentence on a slip of paper, cut it into individual words, mix them up.
Challenge: can they rebuild it before you count to 20?
Grammar review disguised as a scramble race. 🏁

body:
Kids learning to build sentences often need to hear the same structure over and over — not because they forgot, but because they're testing whether it still works the same way.
That repetition is the point. They're running the pattern until it feels solid enough to trust.
Consistency before complexity, every time.
